body.statement:
Suppose \(\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\) and \(h\in\mathbb R\).  Then \((\eta,h)\in\mathcal G_{\mathrm{stab}}\): the set \(\mathcal S(\eta,h)\) is always a separated singleton.  Its member \(x_\star(\eta,h)\) is given by the following explicit scalar map.  If \(h=0\), then \(x_\star(\eta,0)=0\).  If \(h\neq0\), define
\[
 s=\operatorname{sgn}(h\mu_a\mu_b),\quad
 z_0=\kappa|h\mu_a\mu_b|,\quad
 b_0=\kappa|h\mu_a|\sqrt{v_b},\quad
 c_0=\kappa|h\mu_b|\sqrt{v_a},\quad
 d_0=\kappa|h|\sqrt{v_av_b},
\]
and, for \(0\leq z\leq z_0\), put
\[
 w=z_0-z,\qquad Q(z)=z^2+b_0^2+c_0^2+d_0^2,
\]
\[
 \tau(z)=\frac{Q(z)+\sqrt{Q(z)^2-4d_0^2w^2}}2,qquad
 \mathcal R(z)=\frac{d_0^2w\tau(z)\{\tau(z)+zw\}}
 {z\tau(z)+d_0^2w}.
\]
Let \(z_\star=0\) when \(\tau(0)^2\leq c\); when \(\tau(0)^2>c\), let \(z_\star\) be the unique root of \(\mathcal R(z)=c\) in \((0,z_0)\).  Then
\[
 \mathcal S(\eta,h)=\{x_\star(\eta,h)\},\qquad
 x_\star(\eta,h)=\frac{s}{\kappa}(z_0-z_\star).
\]
The map \((\eta,h)\mapsto x_\star(\eta,h)\) is continuous.  For every compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times\mathbb R\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
 \inf_{(\eta,h)\in\mathcal K}\ \inf_{|x-x_\star(\eta,h)|\geq\varepsilon}
 \left\{\Phi_{\eta,h}(x)-\Phi_{\eta,h}\bigl(x_\star(\eta,h)\bigr)\right\}>0. \tag{8}
\]
Consequently, let \((\eta_n,h_n)\in\mathcal K\), let \(C_n:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) be random criteria, and let \(\widehat x_n\) be any measurable global minimizer.  If \(\widehat x_n\) is uniformly tight and, for every finite \(M\),
\[
 \sup_{|x|\leq M}\left|
 \{C_n(x)-C_n(x_\star(\eta_n,h_n))\}
 -\{\Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}(x)-\Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}(x_\star(\eta_n,h_n))\}
 \right|\xrightarrow{p}0,
\]
then \(\widehat x_n-x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\xrightarrow{p}0\).  Thus no coefficient-indexed next-order noise process is needed to break a first-order tie.

The critical selection is one-sided but remains unique.  At a point with \(h\neq0\) and \(\tau(0)^2=c\), consider any admissible path indexed by \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) for which
\[
 \Delta_\epsilon=\tau_\epsilon(0)^2-c_\epsilon
 =\epsilon\dot\Delta+o(\epsilon).
\]
Writing \(\mathcal R_0'(0)<0\) for the derivative at the limiting point, one has
\[
 z_{\star,\epsilon}
 =\epsilon\frac{(\dot\Delta)_+}{-\mathcal R_0'(0)}+o(\epsilon),
\qquad
 x_{\star,\epsilon}-h_\epsilon\mu_{a,\epsilon}\mu_{b,\epsilon}
 =-\frac{s}{\kappa}\epsilon
 \frac{(\dot\Delta)_+}{-\mathcal R_0'(0)}+o(\epsilon).
\]
In particular, opposite admissible \(m^{-1/4}\) drifts can change this local directional derivative, but both selections converge to the same critical minimizer; they cannot produce different separated limiting selections with identical limiting nuisance coordinates.
body.proof_tex:
Because \(\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\), the coordinates \(c,p,q,v_a,v_b\) are strictly positive, \(\mu_a\mu_b\neq0\), and
\[
 \kappa=\sqrt{\max\{c,1\}pq}>0.
\]
First suppose \(h\neq0\), and define the orthogonal sign matrices
\[
 U=\operatorname{diag}\{\operatorname{sgn}(\mu_a),1\},
 \qquad
 V=\operatorname{diag}\{\operatorname{sgn}(h\mu_b),\operatorname{sgn}(h)\}.
\]
Writing \(s=\operatorname{sgn}(h\mu_a\mu_b)\), direct substitution in the definition of \(B_{\eta,h}(x)\) gives
\[
 UB_{\eta,h}(x)V
 =\begin{pmatrix}z&b_0\\c_0&d_0\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad z=z_0-s\kappa x,
\]
where
\[
 z_0=\kappa|h\mu_a\mu_b|,
 \quad b_0=\kappa|h\mu_a|\sqrt{v_b},
 \quad c_0=\kappa|h\mu_b|\sqrt{v_a},
 \quad d_0=\kappa|h|\sqrt{v_av_b}.
\]
All of \(b_0,c_0,d_0,z_0\) are strictly positive, and
\[
 \frac{b_0c_0}{d_0}=z_0.
\]
Left and right multiplication by orthogonal matrices preserves the Frobenius norm and every singular value.  Moreover, \(x\mapsto z_0-s\kappa x\) is a bijection of \(\mathbb R\).  Thus \(\Phi_{\eta,h}(x)\) is exactly the scalar criterion in \(\text{lem:scalar-profile-singleton}\), with \(\rho=c\), under this affine change of coordinate.  That lemma proves that the unique global minimizer is \(z_\star=0\) when \(\tau(0)^2\le c\), and otherwise is the unique \(z_\star\in(0,z_0)\) satisfying \(\mathcal R(z_\star)=c\).  Inverting the affine change gives
\[
 x_\star(\eta,h)=\frac{s}{\kappa}(z_0-z_\star).
\]
Since \(sz_0/\kappa=h\mu_a\mu_b\), this also shows that the minimizer equals \(h\mu_a\mu_b\) in the first case and lies strictly between \(0\) and \(h\mu_a\mu_b\), in the signed direction, in the second case.

If \(h=0\), then \(B_{\eta,0}(x)=-\kappa xe_{11}\).  When \(\kappa^2x^2\le\sqrt c\), the definition of \(\psi_c\) yields
\[
 \Phi_{\eta,0}(x)=\kappa^2x^2-(1+\sqrt c)^2,
\]
whose unique minimum on this region is attained at \(x=0\).  When \(\kappa^2x^2>\sqrt c\), it yields
\[
 \Phi_{\eta,0}(x)=-(1+c)-\frac{c}{\kappa^2x^2}
 >-(1+\sqrt c)^2=\Phi_{\eta,0}(0).
\]
Hence \(x_\star(\eta,0)=0\), uniquely.

We next prove continuity and the uniform separation assertion.  The map \((\eta,h,x)\mapsto\Phi_{\eta,h}(x)\) is continuous: the entries of \(B_{\eta,h}(x)\) are continuous, singular values are continuous functions of the entries, and the two branches defining \(\psi_c\) agree when \(s=c^{1/4}\).  Consequently, the profiles converge uniformly on bounded \(x\)-sets whenever their parameters converge.

It remains to control the tails uniformly.  Let \(\lambda_1(\eta,h,x)\ge\lambda_2(\eta,h,x)\ge0\) be the two squared singular values of \(B_{\eta,h}(x)\), and put
\[
 d_0^2=\kappa^2h^2v_av_b,
 \qquad
 S=\kappa^2h^2(\mu_a^2+v_a)(\mu_b^2+v_b).
\]
The rank-one identity for \(A_\eta\) gives
\[
 \det B_{\eta,h}(x)=-\kappa^2xh\sqrt{v_av_b}.
\]
The quadratic formula for \(\lambda_1,\lambda_2\), together with the fact that \(\kappa\) is bounded away from zero on compact subsets of \(\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\), therefore gives, uniformly on every compact parameter set,
\[
 \lambda_1(\eta,h,x)\longrightarrow\infty,
 \qquad
 \lambda_2(\eta,h,x)longrightarrow d_0^2
 \quad\text{as }|x|\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Indeed, the squared Frobenius norm is \(\kappa^2x^2+O(|x|+1)\), uniformly on such a set, while
\(\lambda_1\lambda_2=\kappa^4x^2h^2v_av_b\).  The outlier branch of \(\psi_c\) hence implies the uniform tail limit
\[
 \Phi_{\eta,h}(x)\longrightarrow d_0^2-(1+c).
 \tag{1}
\]
At \(x=0\), the matrix \(B_{\eta,h}(0)=\kappa hA_\eta\) has rank at most one and its nonzero squared singular value is \(S\).  Subtracting \(\Phi_{\eta,h}(0)\) from the limit in (1) gives
\[
 G(\eta,h)=
 \begin{cases}
 d_0^2+2\sqrt c-S,&S\le\sqrt c,\\
 d_0^2+c/S,&S>\sqrt c.
 \end{cases}
\]
This function is continuous across \(S=\sqrt c\) and strictly positive.  In fact, on the first branch \(G\ge d_0^2+\sqrt c>0\), and on the second branch positivity is immediate.  Thus, on every compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}\times\mathbb R\), continuity gives \(\inf_{\mathcal K}G>0\).  The uniform convergence in (1) then supplies an \(M<\infty\) and a \(g>0\) such that, for every \((\eta,h)\in\mathcal K\) and \(|x|>M\),
\[
 \Phi_{\eta,h}(x)\ge\Phi_{\eta,h}(0)+g.
 \tag{2}
\]
In particular, all global minimizers over \(\mathcal K\) belong to one common bounded interval.

Now let \((\eta_n,h_n)\to(\eta,h)\) and write \(x_n=x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\).  Apply (2) to the compact set consisting of this sequence and its limit.  Every subsequence of \((x_n)\) has a further convergent subsequence.  If its limit is \(\bar x\), local uniform convergence of the profiles and the inequalities
\[
 \Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}(x_n)\le\Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}(y),\qquad y\in\mathbb R,
\]
show that \(\Phi_{\eta,h}(\bar x)\le\Phi_{\eta,h}(y)\) for every fixed \(y\).  The uniqueness already proved forces \(\bar x=x_\star(\eta,h)\).  Hence the entire sequence converges, proving continuity of \((\eta,h)\mapsto x_\star(\eta,h)\), including at \(h=0\) and at the spectral boundary.

Fix a compact \(\mathcal K\) and \(\varepsilon>0\).  If the uniform separation in (8) failed, there would be \((\eta_n,h_n)\in\mathcal K\) and \(x_n\) with
\[
 |x_n-x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)|\ge\varepsilon,
 \qquad
 \Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}(x_n)-
 \Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}\{x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\}\longrightarrow0.
 \tag{3}
\]
If \((x_n)\) is bounded, compactness, continuity of \(x_\star\), and local uniform convergence produce a limiting point distinct from the unique limiting minimizer but having the same criterion value, a contradiction.  If \((x_n)\) is unbounded along a subsequence, (2) and
\(\Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}\{x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\}\le\Phi_{\eta_n,h_n}(0)\) bound the difference in (3) below by \(g>0\), again a contradiction.  This proves (8), and in particular every parameter point belongs to \(\mathcal G_{\mathrm{stab}}\).

For the stated stochastic consequence, let \(\varepsilon>0\) and use (8) to denote the corresponding uniform deterministic gap by \(g_\varepsilon>0\).  Uniform tightness permits choosing \(M\) so that \(\widehat x_n\in[-M,M]\) with probability tending to one; enlarge \(M\) so that all \(x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\) also lie in that interval.  On the event that the displayed centered criterion approximation in the theorem is smaller than \(g_\varepsilon/2\) uniformly on \([-M,M]\), no point in that interval at distance at least \(\varepsilon\) from \(x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\) can have criterion value no larger than the value at \(x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)\).  Since \(\widehat x_n\) is a global minimizer, it follows that
\[
 \Pr\{|\widehat x_n-x_\star(\eta_n,h_n)|\ge\varepsilon\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus a next-order selector is unnecessary.

Finally, fix a critical point with \(h\neq0\) and \(\tau(0)^2=c\).  We first verify the derivative sign used in the expansion.  At \(z=0\), let \(t=\tau(0)\), let \(u\) be the smaller squared singular value of \(M(0)\), and let \(w=z_0\).  Then
\[
 t+u=Q(0),\qquad tu=d_0^2w^2,
\]
and the nonzero off-diagonal entry of \(M(0)^{\top}M(0)\) makes \(t>u>0\).  Differentiating
\[
 \tau(z)^2-Q(z)\tau(z)+d_0^2w(z)^2=0
\]
at zero, using \(Q'(0)=0\) and \(w'(0)=-1\), yields
\[
 \tau'(0)=\frac{2d_0^2w}{t-u}.
\]
Since \(\mathcal R(0)=t^2\), logarithmic differentiation of the displayed formula for \(\mathcal R\) gives
\[
 \frac{\mathcal R'(0)}{\mathcal R(0)}
 =\frac{2\tau'(0)}t+\frac wt-\frac{t}{d_0^2w}
 =\frac{4u}{w(t-u)}-\frac{w(t-u)}{tu}.
 \tag{4}
\]
Furthermore,
\[
 M(0)^{\top}M(0)
 =\begin{pmatrix}c_0^2&c_0d_0\\c_0d_0&b_0^2+d_0^2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Its smaller eigenvalue satisfies \(u<c_0^2\), since the Rayleigh quotient at the first coordinate vector is \(c_0^2\) and that vector is not an eigenvector because \(c_0d_0>0\).  Hence
\[
 (t-u)^2-4d_0^2u
 =(c_0^2-b_0^2-d_0^2)^2+4d_0^2(c_0^2-u)>0.
\]
Using \(tu=d_0^2w^2\), this strict inequality is equivalent to the right-hand side of (4) being negative.  Therefore \(\mathcal R'_0(0)<0\).

Consider now an admissible path converging to this critical point and satisfying
\(\Delta_\epsilon=\tau_\epsilon(0)^2-c_\epsilon
=\epsilon\dot\Delta+o(\epsilon)\).  The identity
\[
 \mathcal R_\epsilon(0)-c_\epsilon=\Delta_\epsilon
\]
and the exact selection rule show that \(z_{\star,\epsilon}=0\) whenever \(\Delta_\epsilon\le0\).  Whenever \(\Delta_\epsilon>0\), the selected root obeys
\[
 0=\mathcal R_\epsilon(z_{\star,\epsilon})-c_\epsilon.
\]
Continuity of the minimizer, already proved, gives \(z_{\star,\epsilon}\to0\).  The mean-value theorem and continuity of \(\mathcal R_\epsilon'\) near zero therefore yield
\[
 z_{\star,\epsilon}
 =\epsilon\frac{(\dot\Delta)_+}{-\mathcal R'_0(0)}+o(\epsilon).
\]
Because the limiting \(h\), \(\mu_a\), and \(\mu_b\) are nonzero, \(s_\epsilon=s\) for all sufficiently small \(\epsilon\), while \(\kappa_\epsilon\to\kappa\).  The exact inverse-coordinate identity
\[
 x_{\star,\epsilon}-h_\epsilon\mu_{a,\epsilon}\mu_{b,\epsilon}
 =-\frac{s_\epsilon}{\kappa_\epsilon}z_{\star,\epsilon}
\]
then proves the asserted second expansion.  In particular, taking \(\epsilon=m^{-1/4}\) changes only a term that vanishes without this additional rescaling.  Opposite local drifts can therefore change the directional derivative but, by continuity and uniqueness, cannot yield distinct separated limiting selections at the same limiting nuisance coordinates.
